commit.message:
feat: notify relay on QUARANTINE for reversible enforcement (#133)

* refactor(publisher): add automated source mode + export CATEGORY_LABELS

publishLabelEvent now accepts {source: 'human-moderator' | 'automated'};
metadata.verified flips false for automated sources, content text adapts.
Adds mockRelay injection mirroring publishToFaro for testability.
Exports CATEGORY_LABELS so callers can pick the canonical label name
without duplicating the table.

Standalone polish; no caller changes. Sets up the relay-quarantine
enforcement work without coupling to its architecture.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: notifyRelay() helper for relay quarantine enforcement

Pairs with notifyBlossom: same {success, skipped, error} shape, same
fire-and-forget failure mode at call sites. Maps action transitions
onto funnelcake's quarantine admin endpoint:

- QUARANTINE → POST   /api/moderation/quarantine     (add to set)
- SAFE / AGE_RESTRICTED → DELETE /api/moderation/quarantine/{event_id}
- PERMANENT_BAN → skip (NIP-09 delete already removes the event)
- REVIEW       → skip (internal-only state)
- no event_id  → skip with reason

Outbound NIP-98 token (kind 27235) signed with NOSTR_PRIVATE_KEY,
including a payload-tag sha256 hash on bodied requests. event_id is
validated as 64-char lowercase hex on every call so a malformed id
never reaches the relay.

Reuses the existing nostr-tools / @noble/hashes deps. fetcher is
injectable for tests.

11 unit tests (vitest) cover: skip cases, POST/DELETE shape, NIP-98
token contents (u, method, payload tags), HTTP-level and network-level
errors, and id validation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: notify relay on QUARANTINE/clear in handleModerationResult and admin moderate paths

Wires notifyRelay() into three call sites, paired with the existing
notifyBlossom() calls so manual + automated moderation transitions
flip funnelcake's quarantined_events_set symmetrically:

- handleModerationResult (queue path): uses result.nostrContext.eventId
- /admin/api/moderate: extends the D1 SELECT to pull event_id and uses it
- /api/v1/moderate: looks up event_id from D1 post-write (request body
  doesn't carry it) and reports relay_notified in the JSON response

Failure handling matches notifyBlossom's: log a warning, don't fail the
whole moderation. PERMANENT_BAN remains handled by NIP-09 delete; the
notifier short-circuits on it internally.

All 1144 tests pass; no test changes needed (existing tests don't
configure FUNNELCAKE_ADMIN_URL, so notifyRelay correctly skips).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: tighten QUARANTINE DM template — 24h SLA + author-still-sees note

Updates the QUARANTINE branch in selectTemplate() to:
- explicitly mention the 24-hour human review SLA
- reassure the creator that the video is still visible to them via the
  direct link / their own profile while it's hidden from public feeds

Without this the relay-side hide otherwise looks like a silent
shadow-ban from the creator's perspective.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: FUNNELCAKE_ADMIN_URL for relay quarantine notifier

Production points at relay.divine.video. Empty string disables
relay-side enforcement (notifyRelay returns skipped, broadly safe).

NOSTR_PRIVATE_KEY (already configured) signs the NIP-98 token; the
matching pubkey 81549b…cd2898 is already in ADMIN_PUBKEYS for
funnelcake-api production via divine-iac-coreconfig.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: DM creator on auto-QUARANTINE with under-review template

Two coordinated changes:

(1) QUARANTINE template now states the 24-hour SLA explicitly and tells
the creator the video is still visible to them via direct link / their
profile. Without that, the relay-side hide reads as a silent shadow-ban.

(2) handleModerationResult (queue path) now sends a DM on QUARANTINE.
Manual admin-moderate QUARANTINEs intentionally still don't DM — that's
existing product policy preserved by the "DM exclusion for QUARANTINE
via admin moderate" test in src/index.test.mjs.

dm-sender.test.mjs now asserts the 24h SLA and "your profile / direct
link" reassurance is present in the QUARANTINE template; two existing
tests that pinned the old "temporarily hidden" wording updated to
match. 53/53 dm-sender tests pass; full 1144 suite green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: backfill script — sync existing QUARANTINE rows into relay set

scripts/backfill-quarantine-relay.mjs reads QUARANTINE rows with non-null
event_id from prod D1 (via wrangler d1 execute --remote), then calls
notifyRelay() with action='QUARANTINE' for each row to add it to
funnelcake's quarantined_events_set.

- --dry-run prints actions without making calls
- --limit N caps run size (useful for staged rollout)
- --concurrency tunes parallelism (default 5; chunks throttle 250ms)
- Resumable: writes scripts/.backfill-quarantine-relay.checkpoint;
  reruns skip already-processed sha256s
- Lazy node:* imports so the script's pure helpers (parseArgs,
  processChunk) stay importable from vitest workerd tests

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
feat: report-only review (no pre-moderation of uploads) (#134)

* feat: pivot to report-only review (no pre-moderation of uploads)

Stops queueing every new upload for manual review. Content is playable by
default; the team queue surfaces ONLY items a user has reported via
POST /api/v1/report (1984/NIP-56 style).

Behavior:
- /api/v1/scan + /api/v1/batch-scan: no longer enqueue moderation. Response
  body now includes {queued: false, reason: 'reactive_moderation'}.
- relay-poller cron: no longer enqueues new Nostr video events. Still logs
  observed events for telemetry (status: 'reactive_skip').
- /api/v1/report: writes a moderation_results row directly (bypassing the
  queue/pipeline since the team is already going to look). Branches by type:
  - NSFW report types (nudity, porn, nsfw, sexual, explicit, adult, etc.)
    → action: AGE_RESTRICTED + provider: 'user-report'. Auto age-gates while
    pending team confirmation.
  - All other report types → action: REVIEW + provider: 'user-report'.
  - AI report types still record an ai_detection_event for telemetry.
- Both land in the dashboard's existing FLAGGED filter
  (action IN REVIEW/AGE_RESTRICTED/PERMANENT_BAN AND reviewed_by IS NULL).

Conflict resolution on existing rows: PERMANENT_BAN preserved; only
upgrades action when stricter (SAFE→REVIEW, SAFE/REVIEW→AGE_RESTRICTED).

Tests: 804 pass / 0 fail. New: isNsfwReportType helper, NSFW report writes
AGE_RESTRICTED row, non-NSFW report writes REVIEW row, scan/batch-scan no
longer queue.

Cost shape: T&S queue load shifts from ~upload-volume per day to
~report-volume per day. Hive billing remains zero (Hive deprecated in PR
#131; PR #132 plumbing left in place but unused).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(review): address C1+I1+I2+I3 from code review on PR #134

C1: ON CONFLICT now preserves moderator-decided rows. When
moderation_results.reviewed_by IS NOT NULL, the action/provider/categories/
moderated_at fields are kept as-is. Subsequent reports cannot overwrite a
human moderator's decision.

I1: /api/v1/report validates sha256 (isValidSha256) and reporter_pubkey
(isValidPubkey), normalizes sha256 to lowercase before storage, returns
400 with specific error messages for malformed input.

I2: NSFW reports now require >= 2 distinct reporter_pubkeys before auto
AGE_RESTRICTED. First NSFW report writes REVIEW; second distinct
reporter promotes to AGE_RESTRICTED. Defends against single-token grief
where one API caller could otherwise mass age-restrict by varying the
reporter_pubkey field. addReport returns distinctReporterCount alongside
the legacy escalate field.

I3: New REACTIVE_MODERATION_ONLY env var. When 'true' (now the wrangler
default), the queue consumer ack-skips every message instead of running
moderateVideo. Drains in-flight queue messages from before deploy
without re-flooding the team's REVIEW queue with manual-review rows.
Reversible via env flip alone.

New tests: malformed sha rejection, malformed pubkey rejection, first
NSFW writes REVIEW, NSFW writes AGE_RESTRICTED only at 2+ distinct
reporters. createDbMock extended with reporterCount config so tests can
simulate multi-reporter scenarios. 807/807 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: spec + plan for moderation dashboard speedup

Five-PR plan to make moderator-facing pages load in <1.5s. Root causes
documented (per-row funnelcake fan-out, missing-column SELECTs,
correlated subquery, uncached aggregations). Two rounds of independent
review; both blocking and important issues resolved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(tests): match new addReport return shape (escalate + distinctReporterCount)

CI failure on PR #134: 3 tests in src/reports.test.mjs used toEqual()
strict deep-equality and broke when the I2 fix extended addReport to
return {escalate, distinctReporterCount} instead of just {escalate}.

Switch to toMatchObject() so the extra field is allowed AND assert the
expected count value at each escalation tier.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
perf: moderation dashboard speedup (kill fan-out, KV-cache stats, untriaged window function, legacy backfill) (#136)

* docs: spec + plan for moderation dashboard speedup

Five-PR plan to make moderator-facing pages load in <1.5s. Root causes
documented (per-row funnelcake fan-out, missing-column SELECTs,
correlated subquery, uncached aggregations). Two rounds of independent
review; both blocking and important issues resolved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: scope vitest discovery to src/ and scripts/

Default vitest test-file discovery walks the entire repo, picking up
duplicate copies of every test from .worktrees/ and .claude/worktrees/
left over from prior work. Run `npm test` and you get hundreds of
redundant test runs plus an unhandled error from a stale-schema
worktree.

Add explicit include + exclude scopes so vitest only sees the
canonical source tree. No production code change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: add composite indexes + lookup_attempted_at column

Adds four indexes that the dashboard's hot-path queries actually need:
- idx_moderation_action_date eliminates the TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
  on the primary list query (verified via EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN).
- idx_moderation_uploaded_by_date supports buildUploaderHistory.
- idx_bunny_events_sha256_received supports the latest-event-per-sha
  CTE that follow-up commits will introduce.
- idx_moderation_unreviewed (partial, WHERE reviewed_by IS NULL)
  speeds up the FLAGGED filter and the pending-review counts.

Adds nullable moderation_results.lookup_attempted_at column for the
backfill cron to track 404s and avoid hammering funnelcake on
permanent misses.

Wires migrations_dir into the BLOSSOM_DB binding so miniflare
(used by @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers) replays migrations on
every test boot — keeps the test schema in lockstep with prod.

scripts/verify-query-plans.mjs runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN against the
remote D1 and fails if any of the four hot queries regress to a
correlated scan or a temp B-tree sort.

No code-path change yet; later commits in this branch will start
using the new indexes and column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: kill per-row funnelcake fan-out in /admin/api/videos

Root cause:
  enrichAdminLookupVideo (src/index.mjs:852) fires
  fetchFunnelcakeLookupVideo whenever eventId/divineUrl/nostrContext
  is null on the row. The list-endpoint SELECT omitted event_id,
  title, author, content_url, published_at — even though those
  columns have existed since migration 004 — so every card on every
  page render fired one HTTP call to relay.divine.video. With 50
  cards/page that's 50 parallel ~1.6s requests, bounded by the
  Workers 50-subrequest cap; perceived dashboard load was 5–15s.

Fix:
- Extract pure buildAdminVideoFromRow helper into
  src/admin/lookup-helpers.mjs. Mirrors buildStoredLookupMetadata's
  nostrContext shape exactly, so response keys are unchanged.
- Widen the SELECT in /admin/api/videos, getAdminLookupVideo, and
  /api/v1/decisions to include the previously-missing columns.
- Replace Promise.all(videoRows.map(getAdminLookupVideo)) with a
  synchronous mapper. Per-page round-trips drop from ~150-250 to ~3.
- Batch uploader_enforcement: one WHERE pubkey IN (?,?,…) query
  for all unique uploaders on the page.

Field-level shape change to acknowledge:
  nostrContext.client and nostrContext.content used to be filled
  from the funnelcake response. They are not stored in
  moderation_results. List view now leaves them null. The
  single-video detail endpoint /admin/api/video/:id keeps the
  on-demand funnelcake fetch so opened videos still show those
  fields. Dashboard cards do not surface them.

Tests:
- New: src/admin/lookup-helpers.test.mjs (6 tests, pure helper).
- Updated: src/index.test.mjs > "returns mirrored relay context
  fields..." → "returns stored relay context fields without per-row
  fan-out". Now asserts zero funnelcake calls (regression gate) and
  reads metadata from the row.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: KV-cache /admin/api/stats and /admin/api/ai-detection/stats

cachedStat helper wraps an expensive aggregate compute in a
60s KV cache. Read is blocking; write is non-blocking via
ctx.waitUntil (or awaited inline when ctx is missing — keeps
existing tests that call worker.fetch(req, env) without ctx
working without changes).

?fresh=1 bypasses the cache read but still writes the fresh
value back, which prevents a cache stampede when many
moderators hit Refresh at once.

Stats response shape unchanged; the closure constructs the
same {totalInD1, totalModerated, untriaged, pendingFlagged,
breakdown, pending} object the dashboard already expects.

Tests: src/admin/cache.test.mjs (4 tests) — miss/hit/fresh/
corrupt-cache fall-through.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: untriaged endpoint — window function, parallel KV, Nostr cache

Three changes consolidated into one endpoint cleanup:

1. Replace four hand-rolled correlated subqueries
   (WHERE received_at = (SELECT MAX(received_at) WHERE sha256 = ...))
   with a window-function CTE in src/admin/bunny-events.mjs:
   ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sha256 ORDER BY received_at DESC).
   Backed by idx_bunny_events_sha256_received from migration 009.
   Note: the natural-looking GROUP BY sha256 HAVING received_at =
   MAX(received_at) form returns nondeterministic non-aggregate
   columns in SQLite — only when MAX is in the SELECT does the
   "bare column" rule apply. Window function is correct.

2. Parallelize the moderation-flag KV reads. The old code did
   `for (const row) await env.MODERATION_KV.get(...)` — sequential
   N round-trips. Now Promise.all(rows.map(...)) hits them all at once.

3. KV-cache the per-row Nostr fetch with a 1-hour TTL. The Triage
   list rarely changes its top entries within an hour, and a cache
   miss falls through to the existing fetchNostrEventBySha256 call.
   Untriaged goes from ~50 parallel WS calls to typically 0-3.

Untriaged COUNT(*) wrapped in cachedStat with 60s TTL.

Tests: src/admin/bunny-events.test.mjs (7 tests) — single-sha latest,
order, exclude deleted/error, LIMIT/OFFSET, COUNT distinct, single-row
helper. The order-determinism test seeds two rows with different
hls_url and asserts the helper picks the row with the larger
received_at — this is the test that fails on the GROUP BY HAVING
variant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: backfill cron for legacy moderation_results lookup columns

After PR2 widened SELECTs to read event_id/title/author/content_url/
published_at directly from D1 instead of fetching from funnelcake,
~98% of legacy rows still have those columns null because the
writers only started populating them after migration 004.
runBackfill catches them up: every minute, take up to N rows where
event_id IS NULL, call fetchFunnelcakeLookupVideo, persist the
result. Idempotent (UPDATE WHERE event_id IS NULL), rate-limited
(BACKFILL_ROWS_PER_TICK, default 200), and KV-mutex protected

perf: moderation dashboard speedup (kill fan-out, KV-cache stats, untriaged window function, legacy backfill) (#136)

* docs: spec + plan for moderation dashboard speedup

Five-PR plan to make moderator-facing pages load in <1.5s. Root causes
documented (per-row funnelcake fan-out, missing-column SELECTs,
correlated subquery, uncached aggregations). Two rounds of independent
review; both blocking and important issues resolved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: scope vitest discovery to src/ and scripts/

Default vitest test-file discovery walks the entire repo, picking up
duplicate copies of every test from .worktrees/ and .claude/worktrees/
left over from prior work. Run `npm test` and you get hundreds of
redundant test runs plus an unhandled error from a stale-schema
worktree.

Add explicit include + exclude scopes so vitest only sees the
canonical source tree. No production code change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: add composite indexes + lookup_attempted_at column

Adds four indexes that the dashboard's hot-path queries actually need:
- idx_moderation_action_date eliminates the TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
  on the primary list query (verified via EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN).
- idx_moderation_uploaded_by_date supports buildUploaderHistory.
- idx_bunny_events_sha256_received supports the latest-event-per-sha
  CTE that follow-up commits will introduce.
- idx_moderation_unreviewed (partial, WHERE reviewed_by IS NULL)
  speeds up the FLAGGED filter and the pending-review counts.

Adds nullable moderation_results.lookup_attempted_at column for the
backfill cron to track 404s and avoid hammering funnelcake on
permanent misses.

Wires migrations_dir into the BLOSSOM_DB binding so miniflare
(used by @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers) replays migrations on
every test boot — keeps the test schema in lockstep with prod.

scripts/verify-query-plans.mjs runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN against the
remote D1 and fails if any of the four hot queries regress to a
correlated scan or a temp B-tree sort.

No code-path change yet; later commits in this branch will start
using the new indexes and column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: kill per-row funnelcake fan-out in /admin/api/videos

Root cause:
  enrichAdminLookupVideo (src/index.mjs:852) fires
  fetchFunnelcakeLookupVideo whenever eventId/divineUrl/nostrContext
  is null on the row. The list-endpoint SELECT omitted event_id,
  title, author, content_url, published_at — even though those
  columns have existed since migration 004 — so every card on every
  page render fired one HTTP call to relay.divine.video. With 50
  cards/page that's 50 parallel ~1.6s requests, bounded by the
  Workers 50-subrequest cap; perceived dashboard load was 5–15s.

Fix:
- Extract pure buildAdminVideoFromRow helper into
  src/admin/lookup-helpers.mjs. Mirrors buildStoredLookupMetadata's
  nostrContext shape exactly, so response keys are unchanged.
- Widen the SELECT in /admin/api/videos, getAdminLookupVideo, and
  /api/v1/decisions to include the previously-missing columns.
- Replace Promise.all(videoRows.map(getAdminLookupVideo)) with a
  synchronous mapper. Per-page round-trips drop from ~150-250 to ~3.
- Batch uploader_enforcement: one WHERE pubkey IN (?,?,…) query
  for all unique uploaders on the page.

Field-level shape change to acknowledge:
  nostrContext.client and nostrContext.content used to be filled
  from the funnelcake response. They are not stored in
  moderation_results. List view now leaves them null. The
  single-video detail endpoint /admin/api/video/:id keeps the
  on-demand funnelcake fetch so opened videos still show those
  fields. Dashboard cards do not surface them.

Tests:
- New: src/admin/lookup-helpers.test.mjs (6 tests, pure helper).
- Updated: src/index.test.mjs > "returns mirrored relay context
  fields..." → "returns stored relay context fields without per-row
  fan-out". Now asserts zero funnelcake calls (regression gate) and
  reads metadata from the row.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: KV-cache /admin/api/stats and /admin/api/ai-detection/stats

cachedStat helper wraps an expensive aggregate compute in a
60s KV cache. Read is blocking; write is non-blocking via
ctx.waitUntil (or awaited inline when ctx is missing — keeps
existing tests that call worker.fetch(req, env) without ctx
working without changes).

?fresh=1 bypasses the cache read but still writes the fresh
value back, which prevents a cache stampede when many
moderators hit Refresh at once.

Stats response shape unchanged; the closure constructs the
same {totalInD1, totalModerated, untriaged, pendingFlagged,
breakdown, pending} object the dashboard already expects.

Tests: src/admin/cache.test.mjs (4 tests) — miss/hit/fresh/
corrupt-cache fall-through.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: untriaged endpoint — window function, parallel KV, Nostr cache

Three changes consolidated into one endpoint cleanup:

1. Replace four hand-rolled correlated subqueries
   (WHERE received_at = (SELECT MAX(received_at) WHERE sha256 = ...))
   with a window-function CTE in src/admin/bunny-events.mjs:
   ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sha256 ORDER BY received_at DESC).
   Backed by idx_bunny_events_sha256_received from migration 009.
   Note: the natural-looking GROUP BY sha256 HAVING received_at =
   MAX(received_at) form returns nondeterministic non-aggregate

   "bare column" rule apply. Window function is correct.

2. Parallelize the moderation-flag KV reads. The old code did
   `for (const row) await env.MODERATION_KV.get(...)` — sequential

3. KV-cache the per-row Nostr fetch with a 1-hour TTL. The Triage
   list rarely changes its top entries within an hour, and a cache
   miss falls through to the existing fetchNostrEventBySha256 call.
   Untriaged goes from ~50 parallel WS calls to typically 0-3.

hls_url and asserts the helper picks the row with the larger
received_at — this is the test that fails on the GROUP BY HAVING
variant.

commit.message:
fix(relay-admin): fail loudly when Cloudflare Access blocks the worker (#135)

* fix(relay-admin): fail loudly when CF Access blocks the worker

Symptom: moderation dashboard delete button silently failed with
"Event action failed: Relay admin error: HTTP 302" because the worker
had no CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID/CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET secrets and got
bounced to the Cloudflare Access login page instead of reaching
relay.admin.divine.video/api/moderate. Took ~30 minutes of curl + log
spelunking to find the missing secrets — should have been obvious from
the dashboard error.

Three changes (defense in depth):

1. callRelayAdminAction: log a clear console.warn at request time
   whenever CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID/SECRET aren't both set, so the missing
   config shows up in `wrangler tail` BEFORE the first user action
   triggers the failure.

2. callRelayAdminAction: detect a 302 to *.cloudflareaccess.com
   specifically (with redirect: 'manual' so workerd surfaces it) and
   throw a self-documenting error that names the likely cause
   (token missing vs token expired/unauthorized) and points at the
   project memory file.

3. /admin/api/event/{id}/delete: bubble up the underlying failure error
   from relayResult.failures[0].error instead of swallowing it under a
   generic "Failed to delete relay event" message. Dashboard now shows
   the actual root cause string.

Tests: 805/805 pass. New regression test asserts that with no CF Access
secrets and a mocked CF Access 302 redirect, the dashboard endpoint
returns 502 with an error message that mentions Cloudflare Access (not
a generic HTTP 302) AND that a console.warn fires on the missing
secrets.

Setup runbook: see project memory cf_access_relay_admin_secrets.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(relay-admin): point at api-relay-prod.divine.video, not the stale relay.admin.divine.video deployment

Diagnosis from production tail:

The default RELAY_ADMIN_URL pointed at https://relay.admin.divine.video,
which routes to a stale "divine-relay-admin-api" worker deployment
that lacks the NOSTR_NSEC Secrets Store binding required by
handleModerate -> getSecretKey (divine-relay-manager/worker/src/nip86.ts).

Tail of that worker on every dashboard delete attempt:
  TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')

Root cause in nip86.ts getSecretKey:
  const nsec = typeof env.NOSTR_NSEC === 'string'
    ? env.NOSTR_NSEC
    : await env.NOSTR_NSEC.get();   // crashes when binding is undefined
  if (!nsec) throw ...               // defensive check is AFTER the crash

The newer divine-relay-admin-api-prod worker (route
api-relay-prod.divine.video) was deployed with wrangler.prod.toml which
DOES bind NOSTR_NSEC via [[secrets_store_secrets]]. That's the worker
the relay-admin UI actually calls (per VITE_PROD_API_URL). Pointing
the moderation worker at the same host fixes the missing binding by
hitting the working deployment.

Defensive code fix in divine-relay-manager/worker/src/nip86.ts (move
the !nsec check before the .get() call) is a separate followup PR
filed against that repo, since this repo can't fix the relay-admin
worker directly.

After deploy, the user must add the divine-moderation-service service
token to the "Relay Admin API (Production)" Cloudflare Access policy
(it's currently scoped to "admin-tools" wildcard which does NOT cover
api-relay-prod.divine.video — different domain).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
